2 · Paste the post copy

"If the hand count is to check on the machines, then why do we have the machines?" Barbara Haney sponsored Fairbanks Proposition 3.

Did anyone check them? Yes. In 2025 a canvass board hand verified 3,338 ballots, two precincts of 32 plus early voting. The machines came back 100 percent accurate on that sample.

What counted as failure? The ordinance said so up front. A discrepancy over 1 percent. About 33 ballots. The gap was zero.

What does a yes do? Hand counting starts in 2027, so October 6th is still machine tabulated. The ordinance carries no fiscal analysis. A yes locks it for two years, past the Assembly and the voters.

The clerk's ballot title, the tolerance beside the measured gap, Haney's case in full and the five dates still open.

Name the result that would have changed your vote. If none would, what was the audit for?

#FairbanksBorough #AlaskaElections #HandCountAudit

3 · Post, then paste this as the FIRST comment (within a minute)

Editor's note

SCORE 8.52 against a threshold of 7.7 (six revision rounds). Clears the unrelaxed 8.3 as well. No hard fail. Ship. The scorer's one-sentence fix, a stale editor note that still described five rounds and an absent panorama, was applied before ship. One contrast number to see: slide 08's kicker measures 3.6 to 1 at its worst point where the dark band lightens under the last two words; ruled a narrow pass because a kicker is a repeated eyebrow and not primary text and qa.py grades it a warn, but a stricter reader could rule the other way and it is a one line plate fix. Still shipping broken: four frames are a large light rectangle with type plus the new lane, body type is 29 px on slides 03 and 04 against a 32 px floor, alaskaaihq.com is 22 px on slide 09, the standing fixture sits inside LinkedIn's page counter zone on three slides, and the threshold rule is below thumb visibility on several. Best things in it: slide 04's magnifier, where the art parameter and the story reason are the same object; slide 06; the closing question, which asks for a disconfirming result rather than an opinion; and assets/js/akseam.js, which should outlive this deck.
This deck is NOT an artificial intelligence story and it does not claim to be. It runs on this page because it is the same question one layer down, what evidence would persuade a community to let a machine do a public job, and Fairbanks is asking it out loud with a complete record on the table. That framing is written into selection.md. It is NOT stated on slide 2, which carries the clerk's ballot title and nothing about the tabulators, so do not lean on slide 2 in a comment thread. The scorer will ask about it first, so it is flagged here.

Three honesty guards are drawn rather than asserted. The audit's sample scale travels with the 3,338 figure everywhere it appears. The unsampled precincts are drawn behind a drafting break line labelled BALLOT TOTALS NOT DRAWN, NO VERIFIED FIGURE, because the denominator failed verification. The missing cost estimate is an unstruck field on a spec plate with no number, bar or arrow near it.

The fact-checker killed three claims from the original brief, and the copy reflects that. All four turnout figures were unverifiable and were replaced with KUAC's sourced 20 to 25 percent range. An amendment I had briefed as conceding parity does not exist and runs the other way. The 2,706 signatures are a submission total after an earlier petition fell short, not a clean surplus, so no surplus framing appears anywhere.

SIX BUILD ROUNDS, AND WHAT ROUND 3 NEARLY SHIPPED. Three hard fails were
caught by the review rooms and fixed. Slide 08 dropped the word APPLICATIONS
from two absentee deadline rows, on the one slide a voter acts from, which
changed what both rows meant. Slide 07's spec plate placed its field markers
by arithmetic off a rectangle instead of measuring the type, the stamp text
wrapped to five lines, and the never-struck field landed on AMENDABLE . NO, so
the slide argued the inverse of the two claims it was built from. Slide 03's
shipped thumbnail and its full-size render came from two different builds,
because round 3 re-ran render.py and never re-ran assemble.py. All three are
fixed and verified in the pixels.

THE PANORAMA IS NOW REAL, AND IT WAS NOT BEFORE. The artwork ledger declared a
panorama as this deck's continuity device for six rounds while the pixels
carried nothing of the kind, and both the flow room and the scorer found it
independently. Round 6 made it a function rather than an intention, one
continuous curve across all 9720 px of the deck, so the lit lane's height and
slope at the right edge of each slide equal its height and slope at the left
edge of the next, by construction. Verified off the shipped PNGs rather than
by eye, seam by seam. 3 of 8 seams carried a matching lit band before, 8 of 8
now, with peak offsets of 4 to 20 design px. It also gives every right edge the
swipe cue the deck had nowhere, and it gives the four flattest frames the one
compositional event they lacked.

KNOWN SHORTFALLS THAT STILL SHIP. The threshold rule, the red 1 percent line,
is below thumb visibility on several slides, so a reader can't track it as one
object across the deck. Slide 07's lock bar was not dropped or widened, and
slide 03 still has no drafting break symbol at its bar terminal. A bespoke
object was drafted for slide 02 to break its flatness and was REVERTED, because
it read as a metal plate floating on a stage and this deck's art direction is
one continuous medium; that reversion is recorded in the storyboard rather than
quietly dropped. These are the first work of the next run.

SCORED 8.52 AGAINST A THRESHOLD OF 7.7, and it clears the unrelaxed 8.3 as
well. No hard fail. One contrast number is worth your eye before you post.
Slide 08's kicker, THE DATES THAT ARE STILL OPEN, measures 3.6 to 1 at its
worst point, where the dark band lightens under the last two words. Round 6
raised both kickers to a brighter cream and on slide 08 it did not fully take.
The scorer ruled it a narrow pass, because a kicker is a repeated eyebrow and
not primary text, the 64.5 px headline and the 28 px date register on the same
slide are both well clear, and qa.py grades it a warn. A stricter reader could
rule the other way. It is a one line plate fix if you want it.

OTHER THINGS THE SCORER NAMED AND I AGREE WITH. Body type is 29 px on slides 03
and 04, under the 32 px floor. alaskaaihq.com is 22 px on slide 09, under the
24 px floor. DRAWN TO SCALE sits 63 px from the bottom edge on slides 03, 04
and 08, inside LinkedIn's page counter zone. Slide 04's last body line and the
standing fixture touch. None of these blocks the post and all of them are the
next run's first work.

IF SOMEONE PUSHES BACK. The cover reads ZERO DISCREPANCY with the sample scale
on the line directly under it. If anyone takes it for a full recount, the
answer is slides 03 and 06, two precincts of 32 plus the early voting station.
Note that slide 06 prints Thirty were not while slide 03 deliberately refuses
to print a precinct count for the remainder. Both are defensible, the first is
32 minus 2, but do not let the two be argued against each other.

WHAT THE SEAM DOES AND DOES NOT CLAIM. The measurement behind the panorama is
narrow and worth stating precisely. The LIT LANE crosses each of the eight
seams at a matching height, verified peak by peak off the shipped PNGs. The
FRAMES AS A WHOLE do not continue. Phase 12 measured whole-column correlation
across adjacent seams at 0.082 against 0.100 for non-adjacent pairs in the same
deck, which is no continuity at all, and it declined to ship a gate on that
metric because such a gate would fail this deck. Both numbers are true. The
lane is the continuous element and the rest of each frame is its own
composition, which was always the design, but do not read the 8 of 8 as a claim
that the nine frames butt together into one picture. They do not.

OPERATIONS THIS RUN. Site sign-off PASS, 95 pages, 18 of 18 checks clean. Gas
Watch PASS, reading current, 29 days on record with no gaps, chart present, and
the page's numerals all trace to a computation. Docket refreshed to 24 tracked
decisions and the dates check is clean across 278 assertions. No subscriber
alerts were due. One collector is failing and it is not this run's to fix. The
docket watch's `basis-bills` source, the Alaska Legislature's BASIS, returned
HTTP 503 on its sweep, recorded in ledger/watch.json. The Federal Register half
of that sweep worked. If BASIS stays down the docket's legislative eye is half
shut, so it is worth a look if it persists.

Aftercare (this is where reach is won)

  • Post Tuesday to Thursday, 8 to 11 a.m. Alaska time.
  • Paste the first comment within 60 seconds of posting.
  • Reply substantively to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes.
  • If a Fairbanks voter asks what the audit did not cover, the answer is on slide 6 and it is two precincts of 32 plus early voting.
  • If someone asks what hand counting would cost, the honest answer is that nobody has published an estimate.
  • Do not let a commenter turn this into an AI story. It is not one. The deck never says what the machines are, so answer from the selection rationale, which is that this is the same question one layer down, what evidence would persuade a community to let a machine do a public job.
